timing: One quarter note is one second. JSON drives notation, MIDI and transformed audio. Roy retains D4 microtiming.
notation: Sounding output pitches; low and sustained parts are studio transformations, not a playable solo-ukulele transcription.

processing.roy: D4 clean recorded performance, byte-identical stem; screen perspective retained
processing.plucks: Recorded notes; dry -> subtle detuned double / short echoes / saturation
processing.low: C4 recording resampled down to original bass pitches; low-pass and parallel saturation
processing.bloom: Recorded notes phase-vocoder stretched at unchanged pitch; soft swells and growing tremolo
processing.grit: Recorded low chord, stretched and driven through tanh; no brass sample
processing.body: Recorded body-tap and muted-strum articulations; no synthesized drum or shredder in music
processing.reverse: Recorded pluck reversed into the next structural cue

title: All title-note events begin exactly at 166; one attack, no retrigger; decay ends by 170
